findings.claim: The daemon rejected --ca-cert in remote attach and provider modes even though the CA still configures daemon-owned CLI TLS.
findings.evidence: Before the fix, validate_ca_cert_launch_mode rejected external_launch. It now permits the mode and strips ca_cert only before local-browser validation; built CDP and provider commands progress to connection refusal and missing credentials.
findings.path: main -> daemon environment -> handle_launch -> validate_ca_cert_launch_mode -> browser validation

findings.claim: --ca-cert caused CLI-only actions to request an accidental local browser launch.
findings.evidence: Before the fix, should_send_local_launch_config treated any ca_cert as launch configuration. It now consults skip_launch_action; built read succeeds with browserLaunched:false and a focused test distinguishes read from navigate.
findings.layer: CLI dispatch ordering and launch selection

exemptions.evidence: native/stream/chat.rs only replaces reqwest::Client::new with the shared trust-aware HTTP client; protocol, payloads, and user-visible streaming behavior are unchanged.

exemptions.claim: Browser-side CA implementation files need not document --use-system-ca.
exemptions.evidence: ca_bundle.rs, native/browser.rs, and the relevant native/actions.rs passages exclusively load or validate local Chromium CA trust; use-system-ca affects CLI TLS only.

exemptions.claim: Historical changelogs need not add the new option.
exemptions.evidence: CHANGELOG.md and the changelog page record prior releases and are not current global-option inventories.
They name the Debian ca-certificates package.
It consumes the wrapper from native/stream/chat.rs, which now constructs the shared trust-aware client.
